inscriptions.inscription_remark: The Qianlong emperor had unrolled and viewed the scroll in his old age, as indicated by the impression of the seals he used after abdicating in 1796.

inscriptions.inscription:
The eighth month, first year of Qianlong [1736] 乾隆元年八月吉日.
The Empress (Xiaoxian) 皇后 (1712–1748), 
The Guifei (Huixian) 貴妃 (?-–1745), 
Chunfei 純妃 (1713–1760), 
Jiafei 嘉妃 (?–1755), 
Lingfei 令妃 (1727–1775), 
Shufei 舒妃 (1728–1777), 
Qingbin 慶嬪 (1724–1774), 
Yingbin 穎嬪 (1731–1800), 
Xinbin 忻嬪 (?–1764), 
Dunfei 惇妃 (1746–1806), 
Xunfei 順妃 (1749–1788), 
Shunbin 循嬪 (?–1797).
inscriptions.inscription_remark:
The inscription dates Qianlong’s portrait to an auspicious day in the eight month, the first year of Qianlong (1736). He was twenty-six years old and had ascended the throne only a year earlier, following the death of his father the Yongzheng Emperor. 
None of the wives was older than 20 at the time she was painted.

did_you_know: Lingfei 令妃 (1727–1775), the first consort depicted in the maroon or “incense-colored" 香色 robe, was the mother of six of Qianlong’s children, including the future Emperor Jiaqing.
description:
This portrait shows the Qianlong emperor at 26, in the first year of his reign. His likeness is followed by portraits of the empress and eleven consorts. Their portraits document the appearances of the court women around the time when they received their respective imperial titles, which occurred at different stages of the emperor's life. The first three portraits were done by the Jesuit (Roman Catholic) missionary artist Giuseppe Castiglione, whereas the later ones were by Chinese court painters.

Formal portraiture contributed to the affirmation of status and construction of role and identity. This scroll served as both familial documentation and a "mind picture" of the Qianlong emperor, suggesting that his constructed image of emperorship was inseparable from concepts of self and family. It was stored in a carved red lacquer box bearing the original painting title Mind Picture of a Well-Governed and Tranquil Reign (see CMA 1969.32).

creators.biography: Italian Jesuit missionary and painter, who worked in China. He served as an artist at the imperial court of three emperors: the Kangzi, Yongzheng, and Qianlong emperors. He painted in a style that is a fusion of European and Chinese traditions.
